rules.title: Statewide rent cap (Civil Code 1947.12)
rules.requirement: An owner may not raise the gross rental rate over any 12-month period by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged in the prior 12 months. For a tenant who stays in the unit, the rent may be increased in no more than two increments over that 12-month period. The owner may set the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains.
rules.key_value: 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property (any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including units in a mobilehome park), except the listed exempt properties. Applies to rent increases after the initial rent of a new tenancy has been set.

rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or K-12 school; housing under stricter local rent or price control; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable property (such as a single-family home or condo) whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, if tenants received the required written exemption notice; a two-unit property where the owner occupied one unit as principal residence at the start of the tenancy and still lives there, and neither unit is an ADU or junior ADU; a homeowner of a mobilehome.
rules.penalty: An owner who demands, accepts, receives, or retains rent above the maximum is liable in a civil action for injunctive relief, damages equal to the excess, discretionary reasonable attorney's fees and costs, and up to three times the excess for willful, oppressive, fraudulent, or malicious conduct. The Attorney General and city attorney or county counsel may enforce and seek injunctive relief. Actions must be brought within three years.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.interaction_text: (3) Housing subject to rent or price control through a public entity’s valid exercise of its police power consistent with Chapter 2.7 (commencing with Section 1954.50) that restricts annual increases in the rental rate to an amount less than that provided in subdivision (a).
